title: GPU benchmarking field notes — instance sizing & token/watt heuristics
body:
Purpose:
This is a working (raw) note set from the October–January run of GPU microbenchmarks focused on deriving quick heuristics for $/token and performance-per-watt across A10, L4, A100, and H100 instance classes. The goal: provide engineering and product with pragmatic sizing rules for common workloads (chat 2k context, streaming prompts, and batch embed pipelines).

Scope & constraints:
- Models tested: mix of LLM families used in production: small- context 7B-class and mid/large 70–300B variants (quantized where applicable).
- Workloads: single-request streaming (low qps), steady small-batch embedding (128–512 batch), and sustained high-throughput generation (50–200 concurrent streams).
- Metrics collected: tokens/sec, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), power draw (W) measured at GPU card level (where available), average latency P50/P95, and observed memory pressure leading to model fallbacks.
- Cost assumptions: blended cloud instance cost + amortized GPU share. We use normalized $/hour GPU rate: A10 = $0.95/hr, L4 = $1.75/hr, A100 = $3.60/hr, H100 = $6.20/hr (these are internal blended rack rates for a reference region). Update per-contract rates before final pricing.

Methodology summary:
- Warmed caches: each model warmed for 3000 tokens to stabilize KV cache behavior.
- Microbench harness: synthetic prompt generator with variable prefix lengths to simulate production prefix reuse patterns.
- Power measurement: for on-prem A100/H100 boxes we used onboard power telemetry; for cloud instances we used provider reported GPU power quotas and multiplier-based estimates when direct telemetry unavailable. Expect 10% measurement noise on W.
- Quantization: where applicable ran FP16, 4-bit (int4-like) quant variants; recorded token throughput deltas.

Raw condensed observations (representative numbers, not final canonical):
- A10:
  - steady embed batch 256: ~18–22k tok/sec, GPU draw ~95–110W, perf/W ~200 tok/sec/W, $/token ~0.000005 (5e-6) assuming continuous usage and blended cost; good at cost-optimized embed pipelines but limited by mem for large-context models.
  - single-stream gen (2k context, 1 request): ~90–110 tok/sec, draw ~100W, perf/W ~1.0–1.1 tok/sec/W (note: lower absolute than A100/H100 on generative tasks).
- L4:
  - steady embed batch 256: ~28–34k tok/sec, draw ~120–140W, perf/W ~240 tok/sec/W, $/token ~0.000004; better than A10 for embed throughput and slightly higher power but better perf per dollar for mid-volume.
  - single-stream gen (2k): ~150–210 tok/sec, draw ~140W, perf/W ~1.1–1.5 tok/sec/W; good latency for small-to-mid models.
- A100 (80GB class typical):
  - steady embed batch 512: ~95–120k tok/sec, draw ~300–350W, perf/W ~320 tok/sec/W, $/token ~0.0000017; excellent for large-scale batch embed and high-concurrency generation.
  - sustained multi-stream gen (100 concurrent small streams): sustained ~55–75k tok/sec aggregate, draw ~320W, perf/W high; memory headroom allows larger LMs and longer contexts.
- H100 (PCIe/stock depending):
  - steady embed batch 512: ~110–150k tok/sec, draw ~350–420W, perf/W ~330–360 tok/sec/W, $/token ~0.0000013; best raw perf/dollar for extremely high-throughput workloads where H100-specific kernels (tensor float, sparse kernels) are leveraged.
  - single high-capacity model (very long context, >8k) performs notably better due to memory bandwidth and kernel optimizations.

Quick calculations & canonical formulas used here:
- tokens_per_dollar = (tokens/sec * 3600) / (instance_gpu_hourly_cost)  // for single-GPU equivalence
- $/token = 1 / tokens_per_dollar
- perf_per_watt = tokens/sec / average_gpu_watts
Note: if instance has N GPUs, divide hourly cost by N to get per-GPU cost in these heuristic calcs.

Example back-of-envelope numbers (from the above obs & blended rates):
- A10 single-stream gen: tokens/sec 100 -> tokens/hr = 360k; GPU cost/hr = $0.95 -> tokens_per_dollar = 360k / 0.95 = ~379k; $/token ~ 2.64e-6 (BUT we observe dropped perf with multi-tenant CPU contention so add 15–20% safety factor for production estimates).
- A100 batch embed: tokens/sec 110k -> tokens/hr 396M; GPU cost/hr = $3.60 -> tokens_per_dollar = 396M / 3.6 = 110M; $/token ~9.1e-9 (this indicates why A100/H100 are dominant for massive embedding farms).

Notable tradeoffs & practical notes:
- Latency-sensitive streaming vs. throughput-optimized batching: A10/L4 cheaper at low qps but A100/H100 dominate when batching/parallelism is available. Choose instance class by access pattern: if > 50% of requests can be batched or if embedding pipeline amortizes large batches, prefer A100/H100.
- Quantization increases tokens/sec but sometimes increases token variance and P95 latency; recommend staged rollout and QA to avoid quality regressions.
- Power regressions: in sustained full-chip scenarios A100/H100 can hit thermal throttling depending on host; we observed ~5–10% throughput drops after hours of peak. Include conservative headroom in SLOs.
- Memory-limited models: A10/L4 will fall back to smaller model variants for long contexts; plan fallback policies (shorter context, offload to cache) to avoid costly fallbacks mid-request.

Operational heuristics / rule-of-thumb recommendations (for product and infra teams):
- Embedding farms (high batch, >=128): prefer A100 for cost-sensitive scale or H100 when throughput is the primary axis and you can exploit H100 kernels. If your batch sizes are small/irregular, L4 can be the best middle-ground.
- Low-latency chat endpoints (single-stream heavy): use L4 for mid-size models; A10 only for extremely cost-constrained scenarios or embed-only.
- Mixed workloads: route cold/rare requests to A10/L4 and hot/steady batched jobs to A100/H100 via smart routing policies. Use caching + request shaping to maximize batch efficiency.
- Autoscale knobs: favor adding more A100 GPUs for capacity rather than over-provisioning many A10s when you need consistent high throughput; for bursty low-latency add small L4-backed fast lanes.

What we still need (action items):
- Repeat same suite with standardized end-to-end token accounting (include CPU, network egress if applicable) for final canonical $/token by model size. (Assigned: Liang)
- Add telemetry hooks to measure per-container GPU wattage in cloud regions (ask infra to enable telemetry exports). (Assigned: Carlos)
- Run cross-quantization quality evals for 4-bit variants to estimate user-facing quality delta per token saved. (Assigned: Amira)
- Draft routing policy examples (cost-first, latency-first, hybrid) with simulated costs using the heuristics in this note. (Assigned: product-optimize squad)

Appendix: quick shorthand table (human readable)
Class | typical tokens/sec (representative) | avg GPU W | perf/W | blended $/hr (GPU) | rough $/token (continuous)
A10   | 100 (gen) / 20k (embed)             | 100W     | 200 tok/W | $0.95/hr           | ~2.6e-6 (gen) / ~5e-6 (embed)
L4    | 180 (gen) / 30k (embed)             | 140W     | 214 tok/W | $1.75/hr           | ~1.9e-6 / ~4e-6
A100  | 3–120k (varies by mode)              | 320W     | 320 tok/W | $3.60/hr           | ~1.7e-6 (gen) / ~1.9e-7 (embed high batch)
H100  | 4–150k (varies)                     | 380W     | 360 tok/W | $6.20/hr           | ~1.3e-6 (gen) / ~1.2e-7 (embed high batch)

Final note (tone): these are field notes — not canonical. Use the formulas and operational heuristics here to run final sims with your own contracted GPU rates and model-specific tokenization characteristics. Ping me (Priya) or Liang for clarifications; we'll fold validated numbers into the product optimize canonical sheet once the remaining action items are closed.
